# AgentScout

> AgentScout is a curated directory of 1,671 AI agent tools for builders and ready-to-use products. Facts are verified; pricing is as makers state it.

Site: https://agentscouthq.com/
X: https://x.com/AgentScoutHQ
Contact: support@agentscouthq.com

- [tools.json](https://agentscouthq.com/tools.json): full catalog

## Recently added
- [All new tools, last 30 days](https://agentscouthq.com/new.html)
- Tools added in the last 2 days (2026-10-21 to 2026-10-22): 71

- [Cayu](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/cayu.html) (added 2026-10-22): Cayu is an open-source Python framework for building and running domain-specific, long-horizon agents on a durable runtime. Sessions survive restarts and redeploys from SQLite or Postgres stores, tool policies can require human approval before side effects, spend caps are checked before each model call, and timers, background tasks, subagents and forks cover longer multi-agent work. It is Apache 2.0 licensed.
- [Diagrid Catalyst MCP](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/diagrid-catalyst-mcp.html) (added 2026-10-22): The Diagrid Catalyst MCP server lets AI coding agents build and operate Dapr Workflows and Dapr durable agents on Diagrid Catalyst, the managed platform for long-running, fault-tolerant agent and workflow apps. Through it an agent can create and inspect workflows, check running instances and manage Catalyst resources from your MCP client. It is the official server from Diagrid, the company behind Dapr, and needs a Catalyst sign-in.
- [FableCut](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/fablecut.html) (added 2026-10-22): FableCut is a Premiere-style video editor that runs entirely in the browser and exposes the whole timeline as one JSON document, covering media, clips, tracks, effects, keyframes and transitions. You can edit by hand or let an AI agent such as Claude Code or Claude Desktop cut the video over MCP or REST while the timeline updates live. It has no npm dependencies, starts with one node command and is MIT licensed.
- [Foreman](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/foreman.html) (added 2026-10-22): Foreman from ThruWire supervises coding agents with fast decision models. You give it a ticket, spec or bug report and it runs Codex, OpenCode, Hermes or LangChain's Deep Agents Code as workers, or attaches to supported sessions such as Pi, then independently judges whether the job meets the original requirements, whether the test evidence is enough and when verification or human input is needed. Extra checks can be configured for your workflow, and it is MIT licensed.
- [Wisp Science](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/wisp-science.html) (added 2026-10-22): Wisp Science is an open-source, local-first AI research workbench for scientists on Windows, macOS and Linux. Its agent searches the literature, runs persistent Python and R kernels on your laptop or remote servers, queries about 80 scientific databases and loads reusable skills, while keeping figures, runs, decisions and drafts together in one project. You bring your own OpenAI-compatible or Anthropic model, or drive Codex or Claude Code, and approval gates stay on by default.
- [OpenHarness](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/openharness.html) (added 2026-10-22): OpenHarness from Autonomous is a native command center for running coding agents side by side, including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Devin, Amp and Copilot. It links your laptop, home server and GPU box into one window with a password instead of SSH keys or port forwarding, keeps code and keystrokes end-to-end encrypted through its relay, and is keyboard first. Agents keep working when you close it, and it extends beyond code to CAD, circuits, robots, games and music.
- [AOCI-CODE](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/aoci-code.html) (added 2026-10-22): AOCI-CODE keeps a persistent, Git-versioned map of your whole codebase and database schema that your coding agent writes and a local MCP server governs. Agents in Codex, Claude Code, Cursor or OpenCode read the map once and know what each file is for, what it depends on and what must not break, instead of re-reading the repo on every task. It can index an existing codebase of up to about half a million lines and report how well it knows each area before taking over development.
- [MemoraX Code](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/memorax-code.html) (added 2026-10-22): MemoraX Code is a shared memory layer for coding agents such as Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor, Trae and DeepSeek Harness. It recalls prior engineering knowledge, captures lessons from finished work, keeps repository knowledge and architecture history up to date, and carries your procedures and preferences into new sessions, bringing back only the memory relevant to the task at hand. It needs Node.js 20 or later and is MIT licensed.
- [Unreal Agent](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/unreal-agent.html) (added 2026-10-22): Unreal Agent is an async-first agent harness from Unreal Labs, a team researching how to make agentic workflows efficient. The library handles inputs with stable IDs and deduplication, append-only sessions that can be forked, and a coordinator that manages each model turn and translates tool calls into operations. It ships with a cloud agent runner, a terminal UI and benchmark runners, under the MIT license.
- [OmniRush](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/omnirush.html) (added 2026-10-22): OmniRush is a desktop coding agent for Windows, macOS and Linux, with a terminal CLI as well. It works through the files of your own projects, reading code, making edits and running commands, and gives free access to frontier models from a model picker, with GPT 6 Astra as the default. Builds for each platform are published on its releases page.
- [Mercury 3](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/mercury-3.html) (added 2026-10-22): Mercury 3 is Inception's diffusion language model, which writes many tokens in parallel rather than one at a time, reaching over 1,000 tokens per second on NVIDIA GPUs with a 1M-token context, tool calling and structured outputs. It has an OpenAI-compatible API and is also offered on OpenRouter, Baseten and Vercel, which makes it a fit for voice bots, support agents and browser agents where response speed matters. Pricing is per million input and output tokens.
- [Voxtral 3](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/voxtral-3.html) (added 2026-10-22): Voxtral 3 is Mistral AI's voice agent stack: speech-to-text in 50+ languages with speaker labels and end-of-turn detection, expressive text-to-speech in 35+ languages, and a voice agent SDK built on LiveKit that handles listening, tool calls and speaking in one stream over SIP or WebRTC. You can use it through Mistral's API with EU, US or global endpoints, or deploy it yourself, and it is priced per minute of audio or per character.
- [UseIt Studio](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/useit-studio.html) (added 2026-10-22): UseIt Studio is an AI design agent for things you can hold. You describe what you want in a sentence, it asks the questions a designer would, and you refine any detail by pointing at it. Instead of a flat mockup you get a real, editable design file ready to print, cut and fold, with true dimensions, bleed and dielines, for pins, stickers, gift boxes, pop-up cards, packaging and brand kits. It runs in the browser, and a Windows desktop helper lets you call it up anywhere.
- [BAND](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/band.html) (added 2026-10-22): BAND is an interaction layer for teams running many AI agents alongside people. Agents and humans share one chat-like workspace where they coordinate tasks, exchange context and hand off work in real time, with governance over how agents communicate built in, instead of hand-wiring every handoff. BAND for Developers connects coding agents across your existing development tools so they can work together without you acting as their project manager.
- [Needle](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/needle.html) (added 2026-10-22): Needle is an outbound engine built for AI agents to drive. You connect it to Claude, ChatGPT or Grok and describe who you want to reach in one prompt; it finds leads from LinkedIn, Instagram and Google Maps, enriches them with context for personal messages, and reaches out from your own connected accounts on whichever channel the lead uses, with sending limits built in. It works for sales, partnerships, hiring or fundraising outreach, and you can start for free.
- [PhoneUse](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/phoneuse.html) (added 2026-10-22): PhoneUse gives AI agents phones of their own to operate. Agents get cloud Android phones that boot in seconds and scale to hundreds, or real retail iPhones and Androids in a San Francisco rack, tapped by a robot stylus, for apps that detect emulators, with real carrier numbers for SMS and 2FA codes. One MCP server with tools such as acquire, read screen, tap, type, swipe, open app and read SMS plugs into Claude, Cursor, Codex or Windsurf, and there is a Python SDK and REST API. On-demand cloud phones are billed per minute, with flat monthly prices for dedicated and real phones.
- [1Password for Agents](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/1password-for-agents.html) (added 2026-10-22): 1Password for Agents lets personal AI agents sign in to your accounts without ever seeing your passwords or one-time codes. When a supported agent reaches a sign-in page, it asks for a credential from your vault; you approve the request, and 1Password fills it straight into the site, so the secret never enters the model or its memory. You can see and manage which agents have access to what. It launched with integrations for agents such as Claude Duet, ChatGPT Work and dots, Meta's Muse and Grok Bot, and needs a 1Password plan.
- [Claude Duet](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/claude-duet.html) (added 2026-10-22): Claude Duet is Anthropic's proactive personal agent app, in research preview. You message it like an assistant: it sends a morning brief from your connected apps, keeps watch on your inbox, calendar and follow-ups through the day, and only pings you when something needs you. You can also hand it tasks, from scheduling meetings to building dashboards or simple web apps, and it keeps working when you step away but checks with you before acting on your behalf. It runs on iOS, Android and claude.ai, starting with a waitlist for US Pro and Max subscribers on their existing plan limits.
- [superagnt](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/superagnt.html) (added 2026-10-22): superagnt is a hosted MCP server and REST API that gives AI agents one key for the tools they lack: Instagram, TikTok, LinkedIn, YouTube, Reddit and X data, web scraping to clean markdown or JSON, email finding and lead enrichment, plus a real Postgres database, memory, schedules, queues and an inbox. Credits are charged only on successful calls, and it plugs into Claude, Cursor, Codex and other agents.
- [GMapsScraper.AI](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/gmapsscraper-ai.html) (added 2026-10-21): GMapsScraper.AI is an AI-powered Google Maps scraper for lead generation: enter keywords and it pulls business listings with names, addresses, phone numbers, emails, social links, ratings, reviews, photos and opening hours, exported to CSV or JSON. It also offers a REST API and a remote MCP server (/api/mcp) so AI agents in Claude, Cursor or OpenAI can run Google Maps searches directly.
- [Metix AI](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/metix-ai.html) (added 2026-10-21): Metix AI (formerly OpenJobs AI) is an AI recruiting platform built around Mira, an AI recruiter agent: you describe the role and Mira searches 900M+ profiles in 190+ countries, runs personalized outreach only after you approve it, handles replies and screening, and books interview-ready candidates on your calendar, often within 24 hours. You still approve outreach and run the interviews.
- [Playable Notes](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/playable-notes.html) (added 2026-10-21): Playable Notes is an AI music tool for piano teachers: snap a photo, screenshot or PDF of piano sheet music and it reads it into a real, playable score, then rearranges it for your student from a plain-language request like "easier left hand", "take out the octaves" or "put it in C". You can hear it, fix any note, print a clean PDF and share practice links, and it also works inside ChatGPT.
- [Moralis MCP](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/moralis-mcp.html) (added 2026-10-21): Moralis's MCP server that gives agents wallet, token, NFT and DeFi data across EVM chains and Solana in plain language.
- [Blockaid](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/blockaid.html) (added 2026-10-21): Onchain security platform used by wallets and exchanges: transaction simulation and scanning that blocks malicious dApps, tokens and signatures before users or agents sign.
- [Messari Copilot](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/messari-copilot.html) (added 2026-10-21): Messari's AI research copilot for crypto, answering questions from its research, news and market data, with an API and hosted MCP server for agents.
- [The Graph Token API MCP](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/the-graph-token-api-mcp.html) (added 2026-10-21): The Graph's Token API MCP server that lets agents query token metadata, balances, transfers and holder stats in plain language.
- [Bitquery MCP](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/bitquery-mcp.html) (added 2026-10-21): Bitquery's hosted, read-only MCP server with 300+ tools for DEX trades, candles, wallet history and money-flow tracing across 40+ chains.
- [Forta Firewall](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/forta-firewall.html) (added 2026-10-21): Forta's pre-execution firewall that screens transactions for exploits and malicious activity and can block them before they settle onchain.
- [Alby MCP](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/alby-mcp.html) (added 2026-10-21): Open-source MCP server that connects a Bitcoin Lightning wallet to your agent via Nostr Wallet Connect, so it can pay and create invoices.
- [Coinbase Agentic Wallet MCP](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/coinbase-agentic-wallet-mcp.html) (added 2026-10-21): Coinbase's MCP server and wallet app (formerly Payments MCP) that let agents hold USDC and pay for x402 services on Base, Polygon and Solana within spend limits you set.
- [thirdweb Nebula](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/thirdweb-nebula.html) (added 2026-10-21): thirdweb's AI for onchain work: agents read live chain data, analyze transactions and can buy, swap and send crypto from connected wallets.
- [Santiment](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/santiment.html) (added 2026-10-21): Crypto market intelligence on on-chain, social and development activity, with an AI assistant and API that agents can use for research.
- [Helius MCP](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/helius-mcp.html) (added 2026-10-21): Helius's MCP server for Solana: agents read accounts, transactions, tokens and NFTs through Helius RPC and APIs.
- [GoldRush MCP](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/goldrush-mcp.html) (added 2026-10-21): Covalent's GoldRush multichain data API with an MCP server, giving agents wallet balances, transactions, token and NFT data across 100+ chains.
- [Dune MCP](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/dune-mcp.html) (added 2026-10-21): Dune's official remote MCP server: agents search on-chain datasets, write and run DuneSQL, fetch results and build charts across 100+ chains.
- [De.Fi Scanner](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/de-fi-scanner.html) (added 2026-10-21): Smart-contract and token scanner that flags honeypots, owner powers and other contract risks, with a credit-based API for apps and agents.
- [ScamSniffer](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/scamsniffer.html) (added 2026-10-21): Real-time intelligence on phishing sites, wallet drainers and scammer addresses: a free browser extension plus a blocklist API teams and agents can query.
- [Webacy](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/webacy.html) (added 2026-10-21): Risk ratings API and MCP server for wallets, tokens, vaults and transactions, so agents can screen addresses and check risk before moving funds.
- [Antalpha Wallet Guard](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/antalpha-wallet-guard.html) (added 2026-10-21): Open-source agent skill that scans EVM wallets for dangerous approvals, malicious addresses, risky tokens and NFTs, rug pulls and phishing sites, powered by GoPlus data.
- [CoinGraph Wallet Guard](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/coingraph-wallet-guard.html) (added 2026-10-21): Checks a swap or send before you sign it: token contract risks, price impact, sanctioned or look-alike recipients. Returns SAFE, WARN or STOP via API or MCP.
- [Tanod](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/tanod.html) (added 2026-10-21): Hosted security MCP and API for agents: pre-transaction checks for token honeypots, risky contracts, phishing URLs, OFAC sanctions, address poisoning, live approvals and wallet drains.
- [GoPlus Security MCP](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/goplus-security-mcp.html) (added 2026-10-21): GoPlus's MCP server that lets agents check token, address, NFT, approval and phishing-site risk before they act, using the GoPlus security API.
- [Guaca](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/guaca.html) (added 2026-10-21): Desktop workspace inspired by Grok Bot where AI agents collaborate, write code and use tools; runs locally or on your own server, with shared conversations, persistent memory and MCP plugins. AGPL-3.0.
- [Akeru Bot](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/akeru-bot.html) (added 2026-10-21): Open-source alternative to Grok Bot for named AI teammates: local-first desktop, web and mobile clients where each bot has its own tools, instructions and memory. MIT-licensed independent fork of T3 Code.
- [Fireply AI](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/fireply-ai.html) (added 2026-10-21): Fireply is an AI agent for growing on X (Twitter): it finds relevant conversations in your niche and writes and posts context-aware replies in your own voice, so you can grow followers, reach and sales without replying by hand. Sign-in uses X OAuth, so it never sees your password, and it also offers free X tools like an account analyzer and advanced search.
- [ClipTalk](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/cliptalk.html) (added 2026-10-21): ClipTalk is an AI video agent that makes finished short-form videos for TikTok, Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts. Give it a prompt, script, product, website, photo or link and it writes the script, generates the visuals, adds a voiceover from 140+ AI voices in 30+ languages, word-by-word captions, B-roll and music, then renders a ready-to-post MP4. You can edit any scene by asking in plain language, clone your own voice, cast AI characters, and on Pro use its API and MCP access for Claude and ChatGPT.
- [Bidhelm](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/bidhelm.html) (added 2026-10-21): Bidhelm is an AI marketing department that runs a company's marketing for it. It researches markets and competitors, writes ad copy and creates ad assets, builds landing pages with lead forms, and runs Google Ads campaigns and X posting every day, managing bids, keywords and budget. It learns from campaign results, moves budget to what works and reports every change it made and why, so owners can steer it in plain language instead of operating ad tools.
- [Reticle](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/reticle.html) (added 2026-10-21): Verification layer for AI coding agents: a dev-only SDK inside your web or desktop app lets the agent drive real flows and read network calls, app state and console, then returns a pass, fail or cannot-tell verdict with the file and line to fix; saved flows replay without an AI model and can gate CI.
- [Sphinx](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/sphinx.html) (added 2026-10-21): Open-source Git hook for agent-assisted coding: before code your agent wrote is pushed to a protected branch, it reads the diff and quizzes you on what the change actually does when things go wrong, and only lets the push through once you answer correctly. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode.
- [trivago MCP](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/trivago-mcp.html) (added 2026-10-21): trivago MCP is trivago's official remote MCP server for hotel search. Ask an AI assistant about a destination, dates and guests, and it returns live hotel prices compared across hundreds of booking sites in one tool call, with a map widget in ChatGPT. It needs no API key and connects in about a minute to Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, VS Code and any client that reads the MCP Registry.
- [WaveSpeed MCP](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/wavespeed-mcp.html) (added 2026-10-21): WaveSpeed MCP is WaveSpeedAI's official MCP server and CLI, which lets an AI agent run any model in WaveSpeed's live catalog of over a thousand image, video, audio and 3D generation models from one connection. Agents can pick a model, submit a generation job and get the result back without switching tools. It is available as a hosted remote server or a local install, and usage is billed per generation at WaveSpeed's API prices.
- [Sundae](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/sundae.html) (added 2026-10-21): Sundae is a personal AI assistant you text from iMessage or Android RCS, with no app or account needed. It works on a computer of its own: it books tables, finds flights at current prices, compares shops, reads letters and photos you send, sets reminders, watches prices and builds simple web pages, then texts back with a screenshot so you can check. It remembers what you tell it, asks before spending money, sending, deleting or opening accounts, and stops at checkout for you to pay. It is free to start with a daily limit, with a paid Plus plan, and is in limited beta.
- [LVLZ](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/lvlz.html) (added 2026-10-21): LVLZ is a personal AI agent you run by messaging it like a person, on iMessage or WhatsApp, as a text, voice note or call. It runs errands on real websites in a cloud browser, such as bookings, forms and shopping, turns messages into tasks and projects, fills a CRM from your conversations, and runs routines like a morning brief or a price watch. Everything it does lands in a web workspace, its memory can be read, edited and exported, and it asks before paying, contacting someone new or deleting anything, with cards and passwords kept in an encrypted vault.
- [Fish Audio](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/fish-audio.html) (added 2026-10-21): Fish Audio is a voice AI platform for text to speech, voice cloning and speech to text, with a real-time API for voice agents. Its Drama 3 and S2 models take inline emotion and delivery tags such as whispering, laughing or pauses, it can clone a voice from a few seconds of audio, and its library has more than two million community voices for narration, characters, audiobooks and support agents. The Fish Speech models behind it are published on GitHub and Hugging Face.
- [OpenComputer](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/opencomputer.html) (added 2026-10-21): OpenComputer is a platform for building and deploying long-running AI agents as code. You define an agent as a TypeScript function with its model, tools and MCP servers, deploy it with one command, and every session gets its own real cloud computer, with managed sessions, schedules and API keys kept outside the agent's runtime. Templates include a coding agent that edits a repo, runs checks and opens a draft pull request, and market-research and GTM agents; its own Slack coding agent runs on it. Pricing is pay-as-you-go for model calls and per-second machine time.
- [onetake](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/onetake.html) (added 2026-10-21): onetake is an agent skill for Claude Code and similar agents that makes product launch films, teasers and feature demos as one continuous camera move, where each beat grows out of the previous one instead of cutting between slides. The agent writes the motion as code and renders it with ffmpeg, and the skill checks continuity at every transition. The free edition on GitHub is for noncommercial use; onetake Pro adds a camera operator that follows each beat, source files for every example film, starter templates and a commercial licence.
- [Concat](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/concat.html) (added 2026-10-21): Concat is a free, open-source video editor meant as a CapCut replacement that runs entirely on your own machine. It covers auto-captions, text-to-speech voices, background removal, keyframes, titles, effects, filters and transitions with multi-track editing up to 4K, with no watermark, account or subscription. It runs on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and iOS, and it can be scripted through a documented JSON-RPC and gRPC API, so scripts and AI agents can drive edits.
- [Tov](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/tov.html) (added 2026-10-21): Tov is an experimental programming language designed to be written by coding agents. It uses TypeScript syntax minus a few traps (no any, null or loose equality, separate int and float types, and failing calls marked with try), so agents already know how to write it, and its compiler returns machine-readable fixes the agent can apply after every edit. Programs compile to small, fast native binaries, with published benchmarks against Rust, Bun and Node. Agents can learn it from the site's llms.txt.
- [Co-op Anything](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/co-op-anything.html) (added 2026-10-21): Co-op Anything lets you point your AI coding agent at a single-player game and have it build or revive a co-op mod, so you can play it with friends online or split-screen. The project gives the agent a step-by-step method for working out what has to be synced between players (the story, enemies, the world, items and players seeing each other) and testing it. Its website is a searchable directory of every co-op mod made this way, with player ratings, how much of each game works in co-op and how active each project is.
- [LayerFS](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/layerfs.html) (added 2026-10-21): LayerFS is a filesystem built for running many coding agents in parallel. Each agent mounts a complete, writable workspace on top of shared committed history, does its work, commits what it changed and goes away, so compute only exists while a command runs. Every tool call becomes a commit on a branch, same-file clashes between agents are refused rather than silently merged, each line records the step that wrote it, and any commit can be forked at no cost for recursive exploration or RL training. Agents on different computers share one serverless store with chunk-level deduplication.
- [IDA MCP (Hex-Rays)](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/ida-mcp-hex-rays.html) (added 2026-10-21): IDA MCP is Hex-Rays' official MCP server for the IDA disassembler and decompiler. It lets AI coding agents and people work on the same IDA databases at the same time, so an agent can inspect functions, types and decompiled code, rename and annotate, and coordinate analysis across several related binaries in one session. It works with the IDA GUI through a plugin or headless through idalib, installs with Hex-Rays' hcli tool, and needs IDA 9.4 or later.
- [Superlog](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/superlog.html) (added 2026-10-21): Superlog runs AI agents on routine engineering work around production. You set up automations with triggers and connectors, for example rating each new Sentry issue, posting a plain-language summary to Slack and opening a pull request with the fix, comparing error rates and latency against their normal range every hour, adding missing logs and spans to hard-to-debug code paths, or answering community questions from your code and docs. You choose the model and agent harness and bring your own tokens or subscriptions. The core is open source (Apache-2.0) with a hosted version.
- [Wake](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/wake.html) (added 2026-10-21): Wake is a desktop app that collects every coding-agent conversation on your computer into one searchable place. It reads the local history kept by Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot CLI, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, Devin and other agents, groups sessions by agent and project, and lets you find a past conversation in seconds and resume it in your terminal. It is read-only and nothing leaves your machine. Built in Rust, it runs on macOS, with Linux and Windows in beta.
- [Hermex](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/hermex.html) (added 2026-10-21): Hermex is a native iPhone and iPad app for controlling a self-hosted Hermes agent. The agent keeps running on your own server; the app connects to it over your private Tailscale network or an HTTPS tunnel, streams replies, lets you answer approval requests, manage tasks and Kanban boards, browse the agent's workspace and get push notifications when it needs you. It is free on the App Store with no in-app purchases, and its source is open.
- [OpenAPPA](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/openappa.html) (added 2026-10-21): OpenAPPA is a deterministic guardrail that sits between an AI agent and its tools and tracks how data flows across tool calls, instead of asking a second model to judge each call. Policies decide whether untrusted or sensitive data may reach a given action, which blocks data exfiltration caused by prompt injection or hallucination while letting agents finish their tasks. It plugs into Claude Code, Pi, OpenCode, kAgent and Archestra, comes with reusable policy "batteries", validation, observability and reporting, and is backed by a NeurIPS workshop paper with published benchmarks. It is in preview as an open RFC.
- [PR Lens](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/pr-lens.html) (added 2026-10-21): PR Lens helps people review code that agents wrote. For each pull request it draws animated architecture and data-flow diagrams inside the PR, showing which parts of the app were added, changed or removed, what else depends on the change and how a request now moves through the system. It also flags likely bugs, security holes and design problems in the same review comment, with a ready prompt to hand each fix to your coding agent or an autofix. The open-source core runs locally and installs as an agent skill.
- [MonoCode](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/monocode.html) (added 2026-10-21): MonoCode is a desktop app that puts the coding agents you already pay for behind one interface. It drives Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Grok Build, OpenCode, Antigravity, Pi, Hermes Agent, Devin and others, using the subscriptions and logins already on your machine, so you never buy tokens through it. Each tab is an agent session and one composer sends work to whichever agent you pick, so several sessions can run side by side. It runs on macOS, Windows and Linux, with an iOS app in public beta.
- [Cumora](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/cumora.html) (added 2026-10-21): Cumora is a team chat app where AI agents are members of the workspace rather than a chat box you prompt. Each agent gets a persona, its own private memory and files, a status, and a schedule on which it wakes up, reads the room and decides whether to message someone, post an idea or pull a small group together. Agents can message each other, and you can read those side conversations. People join by email or link, agents can be grouped into teams and given projects, and the same live workspace runs on desktop, in the browser and on a phone. It is free during an invite-only preview.
- [OpenKnowledge](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/openknowledge.html) (added 2026-10-21): OpenKnowledge is a free, local-first markdown editor and knowledge base built for working alongside AI agents. It looks and feels like a Notion-style WYSIWYG editor, with callouts, tabs, Mermaid diagrams and media blocks, but every page stays a plain markdown file on your disk. Coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI and dozens of others can read and write the same files through its integrations, so specs, team wikis and LLM wikis stay in one place that both people and agents keep up to date. It ships as a desktop app plus a web UI and CLI.
- [Sandbox0](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/sandbox0.html) (added 2026-10-21): Sandbox0 is a managed sandbox runtime that gives each AI agent an isolated cloud computer where it can run code, install software, manage files and control network access. The whole writable root filesystem persists across incremental checkpoints and grows automatically as it fills, so an agent can pause compute between tasks and resume the same sandbox later with its tools, dependencies and files intact. It adds snapshots and restore, SSH, egress proxy and credential injection, private previews, Docker in the sandbox, webhooks, warm pools and custom templates, with integrations for LangChain Deep Agents, OpenAI Agents, Vercel and GitHub CI. Sandboxes run under gVisor isolation with Nomad scheduling.
- [Wren Pre-sign Check](https://agentscouthq.com/tools/wren-pre-sign-check.html) (added 2026-10-21): Wren Pre-sign Check is a pay-per-call x402 API that an AI agent calls before it signs anything with its wallet. Send a transaction (to + data), an EIP-712 typed-data payload or untrusted text, and it returns block, review or allow, the decoded call in plain words and every finding: unlimited approvals, Permit and Permit2 signatures, setApprovalForAll, EIP-7702 delegation, contract deployment and injected instructions. With an optional wren-guard policy (allowlist, spenders, caps) it also blocks unknown recipients, over-cap amounts and lookalike addresses. It is a static check and stores nothing you send; free demos show real output.
